historicalSummary: Saint Michael's Lithuanian parish was established in Scranton's Hyde Park section in 1914, when the city's Lithuanian population had grown too large to be served by one Roman Catholic parish. Its first pastor was Father Adomas Lopata, and the community built a modest wooden church.

Father Jonas Boll-Baltusevičius became pastor in 1933. In 1942 the parish replaced the wooden church with the brick church later known at 1703 Jackson Street. Its Lithuanian fabric included Lithuanian-language parish records and stained-glass inscriptions, including a memorial to Petras and Kotryna Baltusevičius donated by their son.
The parish also built a school with the Sisters of the Crucified Jesus. By spring 1961 it had six grades and 205 pupils; the parish counted 230 families, about 700 people.

A 1972 visit recorded 660 parishioners and 121 pupils, but also a sharp decline in Lithuanian-language life: only a few parishioners could still read and write Lithuanian, and even a Lithuanian Gospel reading drew objections from people who no longer understood it.

As the Lithuanian community waned, the Diocese of Scranton assigned the parish to the Latin Mass community in the late 1990s. The same Saint Michael the Archangel parish continued, later as an FSSP apostolate, and on 28 September 2025 relocated from Jackson Street to Saint Lucy Church. The 1942 Lithuanian-built church now stands vacant and is listed for sale.
summary: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish began as a Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish in Scranton's Hyde Park section in 1914. It first worshipped in a modest wooden church, replaced that building with the brick church on Jackson Street in 1942, and built a school that served 205 pupils by 1961. By 1972 the parish still counted 660 people, but Lithuanian-language life had sharply declined. In the late 1990s the same parish became the home of Scranton's Latin Mass community and later an FSSP apostolate. On September 28, 2025, the parish celebrated its final Mass at 1703 Jackson Street and processed to its new home at Saint Lucy Church, where it continues today. The 1942 Lithuanian-built church and rectory remain standing but vacant and were listed for commercial sale at $350,000 as of July 16, 2026. No regular Lithuanian Mass is documented at the continuing parish.

developments.headline: Final Mass at the former Lithuanian St. Michael Church; parish relocates to St. Lucy's
developments.detail: After several years of growth and increasing space needs, the St. Michael the Archangel parish community (FSSP Latin Mass personal parish) celebrated its final Mass at 1703 Jackson Street on Sept. 28, 2025, then held a Eucharistic Procession through the streets of Scranton to its new home, the historic St. Lucy Church at 949 Scranton Street. Bishop Bambera made the move as part of the Diocese of Scranton's Vision 2030 Pastoral Planning Process; pastor Fr. Anthony Dorsa, FSSP, cited the lack of classroom and gathering space at the Jackson Street site. The Jackson Street church officially closed its doors.

developments.headline: Former church and rectory at 1703 Jackson Street listed for sale at $350,000
developments.detail: The vacated property is an active commercial listing (MLS SC261850): a 4,468 sq ft brick church described as having 'a stunning sanctuary' and built in 1942, a 2,069 sq ft rectory, and a private parking lot across the street, totaling 6,537 sq ft on 0.43 acres. It is marketed as an opportunity for religious organizations, non-profits, businesses, or developers. Listing shown by Lewith & Freeman; 78 days on site as of the July 16, 2026 update, implying a spring 2026 listing date.

developments.headline: Parish continues as FSSP Latin Mass personal parish at St. Lucy's Church
developments.detail: St. Michael the Archangel Parish operates at St. Lucy's Church, 949 Scranton St., Scranton, PA 18504, with all Masses in the Traditional Latin Mass (1962 books): Sunday 8:00 am Low Mass and 10:30 am High Mass, weekday Masses Mon-Thu 7:30 am, Fri 6:00 pm, Sat 9:00 am, plus regular confessions and devotions. Pastor is Fr. Anthony Dorsa, FSSP. The parish name and community survive, but no longer in the Lithuanian-built church.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1977 published parish history resolves the earlier conflict: Saint Michael's Lithuanian parish was established in 1914, first used a modest wooden church, and replaced it with the brick church in 1942. The parish institution later survived the end of regular Lithuanian parish life, became the home of the Latin Mass community in the late 1990s, and relocated to Saint Lucy Church in 2025. The institution therefore survives, while the 1942 Lithuanian-built church is vacant and for sale.
gaps: The later physical disposition of the original wooden church is not established by the supplied pages. The precise date when regular Lithuanian parish life ended and the Latin Mass community assumed the parish remains bounded to the late 1990s. No sale of the 1942 Jackson Street church has closed, so there is no confirmed buyer or sale price beyond the active $350,000 asking price. The fate of its Lithuanian-inscribed stained glass in any future sale is unknown. The public Žiburio archive item URL for the 1977 book scans remains to be added when supplied by Vilija.
